<h>Invitatorium</h>

<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

b.61be36e94a:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Kaléndas Novémbris Luna tricésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>n Sardínia natális sancti Pontiáni, Papæ et Mártyris, qui, ab Alexándro Imperatóre, una cum Hippólyto Presbýtero, in eam ínsulam deportátus, ibídem, mactátus fústibus, martýrium consummávit. Ejus corpus a beáto Fabiáno Papa Romam delátum est, atque in cœmetério Callísti sepúltum. Ipsíus tamen festum recólitur tertiodécimo Kaléndas Decémbris.
<h>Æ</h>géæ, in Cilícia, pássio sanctórum Zenóbii Epíscopi, et Zenóbiæ soróris, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre et Lýsia Prǽside.
<h>A</h>ltíni, in Venetórum fínibus, sancti Theonésti, Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui ab Ariánis occísus est.
<h>I</h>n Africa natális sanctórum Mártyrum ducentórum vigínti.
<h>T</h>ingi, in Mauritánia, pássio sancti Marcélli Centuriónis, qui, sanctórum Cláudii ac Lupérci et Victórii Mártyrum pater, cápitis abscissióne martýrium complévit sub Agricoláo, agente vices Præfécti prætório.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctórum trédecim Mártyrum, qui, cum sanctis Iuliáno, Euno et Macário, passi sunt sub Décio Imperatóre.
<h>C</h>árali, in Sardínia, sancti Saturníni Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Bárbaro Prǽside, cápite truncátus est.
<h>A</h>paméæ, in Phrýgia, sancti Máximi Mártyris, sub eódem Diocletiáno.
<h>L</h>egióne, in Hispánia, sanctórum Mártyrum Cláudii, Lupérci et Victórii, filiórum sancti Marcélli Centuriónis; qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni et Maximiáni, sub Diogeniáno Prǽside, jussi sunt decollári.
<h>L</h>utétiæ Parisiórum sancti Lucáni Mártyris.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctæ Eutrópiæ Mártyris, quæ, Mártyres vísitans, apprehénsa est, et, cum illis sævíssime cruciáta, réddidit spíritum.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ sancti Serapiónis Epíscopi, eruditióne claríssimi.
<h>C</h>ápuæ sancti Germáni, Epíscopi et Confessóris, magnæ sanctitátis viri; cujus ánimam, in hora óbitus ejus, ab Angelis in cælum deférri sanctus Benedíctus aspéxit.
<h>P</h>oténtiæ, in Lucánia, sancti Gerárdi Epíscopi.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.d7e2d954ef:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>O</c>ctober 30th 2027, the 30th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>O</h>n the same day, the holy martyr, Pope Pontian, who was exiled to Sardinia along with the Priest Hippolytus, under the Emperor Alexander, and was there cudgelled to death. His body was brought to Rome by blessed Pope Fabian, and buried in the cemetery of Kallistus.
<h>A</h>t Algaea, in Cilicia, under the President Lysias and the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyrs Zenobius, Bishop (of that see,) and Zenobia his sister.
<h>A</h>t Altino, the holy martyr Theonestus, Bishop (of Philippi, in Macedonia,) who was slain by the Arians.
<h>I</h>n Africa, two hundred and twenty holy martyrs.
<h>A</h>t Tangiers, in Morocco, (in the third century,) the holy centurion Marcellus, who accomplished martyrdom by being beheaded under Agricolaus, Vicar to the Prefect of the Pretorium.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, thirteen holy martyrs, who suffered under the Emperor Decius, along with Julian, Eunus, and Macarius.
<h>A</h>t Cagliari, in Sardinia, the holy martyr Saturninus, who was beheaded under the President Barbarus, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Apamea, in Phrygia, under the same Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyr Maximus.
<h>A</h>t Leon, in Spain, the holy martyrs Claudius, Lupercus, and Victorius, sons of the holy centurion Marcellus, who were beheaded under the President Diogenian, in the persecution under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian.
<h>A</h>t Paris, the holy martyr Lucan.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria also, the holy martyr Eutropia, who visited the martyrs, and, being most cruelly tormented along with them, gave up the ghost.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, (in the third century,) holy Serapion, Patriarch (of that see,) eminent for his learning.
<h>A</h>t Capua, the holy Confessor Germanus, Bishop (of that see,) a man of great holiness, whose soul, at the hour of his death, holy Benedict saw carried heavenward by Angels.
<h>A</h>t Potenza, in Lucania, (in the year 1119,) holy Gerard, Bishop (of that see.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Amen.
